related_questions.question: What do I write in an immigration support letter?

text_blocks.snippet: An immigration support letter should clearly state your relationship to the applicant, highlight their positive qualities and contributions, and explain why you believe they deserve to be granted immigration benefits. It should be a personal statement, not a generic template, and provide specific details and examples to support your claims.
snippet_highlighted_words: clearly state your relationship to the applicant, highlight their positive qualities and contributions, and explain why you believe they deserve to be granted immigration benefits

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed breakdown of what to include:

list.snippet: Start with a clear statement of support for the applicant's immigration case.
Introduce yourself, including your full name, citizenship/immigration status, and your relationship to the applicant.
Briefly explain how long you've known the applicant and the nature of your relationship (e.g., employer, friend, family member).

list.title: Positive Qualities:
list.snippet: Describe the applicant's positive character traits, skills, and contributions. Use specific examples to illustrate these qualities.

list.title: Community Involvement:
list.snippet: If applicable, discuss the applicant's involvement in their community, including any volunteer work or contributions they have made.

list.title: Future Contributions:
list.snippet: Explain how the applicant will continue to contribute to their community and the broader society if granted immigration benefits.

list.title: Hardship:
list.snippet: If relevant, describe the potential negative consequences or hardships the applicant and their family would face if they are not granted immigration relief.

list.title: Relationship Details:
list.snippet: If the letter is for a family member, provide details about the relationship, including how the applicant has contributed to the family's well-being.

list.title: Positive Impact:
list.snippet: Emphasize the positive impact the applicant's presence would have on you and your family, if applicable.
Reiterate your strong support for the applicant's case.
Provide your contact information (phone number and email address) so the immigration authorities can contact you for further information.
End with a closing statement expressing your sincere belief that the applicant should be granted the requested immigration benefit.
If applicable, include a statement that the information provided is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge.
Using generic language or clichés.
Providing information that is not true or accurate.
Making unsubstantiated claims.
Focusing solely on the applicant's needs without highlighting their positive qualities and contributions.

related_questions.question: Do immigration support letters need to be notarized?

text_blocks.snippet: While not always mandatory, notarizing immigration support letters is generally recommended and can add credibility to the document. Notarization helps verify the identity of the person writing the letter and adds a layer of authenticity, which can be especially important in immigration cases.
snippet_highlighted_words: not always mandatory, notarizing immigration support letters is generally recommended

list.title: Notarization is not always required:
list.snippet: USCIS (United States Citizenship and Immigration Services) does not always explicitly require notarization for all supporting documents, including letters of support.

list.title: Notarization adds credibility:
list.snippet: Even if not required, notarization can be beneficial. It provides an extra layer of assurance to immigration officials that the letter is legitimate and the person writing it is who they claim to be, according to some immigration attorneys.

list.title: Notarization may be necessary for specific cases:
list.snippet: In certain situations, such as when the letter includes sworn statements or when requested by the immigration court or USCIS, notarization may be a requirement.

list.title: Affidavits of Support:
list.snippet: Affidavits of support, which are different from general letters of support, often require notarization, particularly if they contain sworn statements.

list.title: What notarization does:
list.snippet: Notarization involves a licensed notary public verifying the identity of the person signing the document and witnessing their signature. This adds a layer of security and authenticity.

list.title: Benefits of notarization:
list.snippet: Notarization can be seen as a way to prevent fraud and ensure the legitimacy of the document.

list.title: Recommendation:
list.snippet: If you are unsure whether to notarize a letter, it is advisable to consult with an immigration attorney to determine the specific requirements for your case.
